planting.note: Set rooted plugs or sod sections into saturated, saline to hypersaline sandy or muddy soil at salt flat, tidal flat, or upper marsh elevations; establishes slowly but spreads steadily once rooted.

directions: Plant divisions or plugs directly into saturated, saline sandy or muddy soil in full sun; shoregrass is a true halophyte of Gulf Coast salt flats, tidal pannes, and the upper edges of salt marshes, where it forms dense, wiry, low mats via extensive stolons and rhizomes. It tolerates hypersaline conditions and periodic desiccation that exclude nearly all other grasses, making it a key stabilizer of bare salt-flat ground between salt marsh and upland coastal prairie. Mow or trim only lightly if used as a low-maintenance salt-tolerant groundcover near brackish water features; otherwise leave undisturbed, as it spreads slowly but persistently once established. Best suited to restoration plantings, living shorelines, and salt-flat demonstration beds rather than conventional lawns.
sources: Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center native plant database

planting.note: Direct sow after soil has warmed in spring; readily self-sows thereafter in sandy, well-drained coastal prairie or dune-edge gardens.

directions: Direct sow in lean, well-drained, sandy soil in full sun after the soil has warmed; this is the widespread mainland subspecies of beach sunflower that ranges along the Texas and western Gulf Coast, distinct from the Florida peninsula's nominate subspecies debilis. Plants branch freely from the base into a sprawling, multi-stemmed mound and bloom continuously through the heat of summer with small yellow-and-maroon daisies that draw bees and butterflies. It thrives in pure beach sand and poor, droughty coastal prairie soil with no supplemental fertilizer, and tolerates salt spray and wind on dune edges and upper beach berms. Deadheading extends bloom, but in a naturalized coastal planting it is usually left to self-seed and reappear each year.
sources: Flora of the Southeastern United States (FSUS)
